lessons.title: Receiving parent seed
lessons.html:
Receiving parent seed

Parent seed is the seed used to plant seed production fields. For a hybrid maize, there are separate female and male parent lines. For self-pollinated crops such as wheat or soybeans, it may be basic seed used to produce certified seed. Parent seed is very valuable and usually available in small quantities. It is also protected by plant breeders' rights. Losing or mixing it can stop a whole season's production.

Before the seed arrives

  • Know what is expected: cultivar or line codes, quantities, lot numbers and expected date, from the production plan.
  • Prepare a clean, cool, dry, secure storage area, separate from commercial seed.
  • Have receiving forms or the system ready.

Receiving steps

  1. Check the delivery note against the order: line codes, lot numbers, number of bags and weights.
  2. Inspect each bag or container. Look for tears, wetness, insect damage, broken seals or missing labels.
  3. Weigh the consignment and compare with the documents.
  4. Check that labels are correct and readable, for example 'female' and 'male' clearly marked for hybrid parents.
  5. Record any difference or damage on the delivery note before signing, and report it to your supervisor.
  6. Capture the receipt in the stock system with location codes.
  7. Store the seed immediately in the secure parent seed store.

Security

Parent seed must be kept locked. Only authorised people may enter the store. Keep a register of who removes seed and when. Never give parent seed to anyone without proper authorisation.

Treated seed

Parent seed is often treated. Wear gloves, do not eat, drink or smoke while handling it, and wash hands afterwards.

lessons.title: Distributing parent seed to growers
lessons.html:
Distributing parent seed to growers

Before planting, parent seed is issued to contract growers according to the production plan. Each grower must receive exactly the right lines, in the right quantities, for their registered fields.

Preparing the issue

  • Get the approved distribution list: grower, fields, hectares, lines, quantities.
  • Check that quantities match planting rates and hectares. Query differences with the production manager.
  • Pick the seed from the store, checking line codes and lot numbers on each bag.
  • Keep each grower's seed together and clearly labelled with the grower's name and field numbers.
  • For hybrids, pack and label female and male parents separately so that the grower cannot confuse them.

Issue documents

DocumentPurpose
Issue noteLists lines, lot numbers, bags, weights; signed by grower or driver
Planting instructionsRow ratios, planting dates, isolation and handling instructions
Label copiesNeeded for field certification

Transport

Load parent seed in a clean, dry vehicle and cover it. Do not load it with fertiliser, chemicals or food. Make sure the person collecting is authorised by the grower.

After distribution

  1. Update stock records immediately.
  2. File signed issue notes.
  3. Record any unused seed returned after planting. Returned parent seed must be checked, counted and stored securely. Growers may not keep or use leftover parent seed.
  4. Report any lost or missing seed at once.

Key points

  • Parent seed is valuable, limited and protected; keep it locked and recorded.
  • Check deliveries against documents and record damage before signing.
  • Issue exact lines and quantities to each grower per the approved list.
  • Pack female and male hybrid parents separately and clearly labelled.
  • Update stock records and recover unused parent seed after planting.
